newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-WILL EL GUERROUJ END MORCELI'S REIGN?.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-WILL EL GUERROUJ END MORCELI'S REIGN?.

text.p: An issue of the authoritative U.S. athletics magazine Track and Field News this year proclaimed: "The king is dead! Long live the king!"
The headline and following report were devoted to 22-year-old Moroccan Hicham el Guerrouj and his two indoor world bests over 1,500 metres and a mile.
And the apparently deceased kings of athletics were Algerian Noureddine Morceli and Ireland's Eamonn Coghlan, who had held the respective records for many years.

Coghlan is now retired from the competitive scene but Morceli is still trying to avoid relinquishing his throne, as the master of middle distance running, to the young pretender from across the Mahgreb.
Morceli has won the world championship 1,500 title on the past three occasions but if he fails to get a fourth gold medal it will probably end up in the hands of el Guerrouj.
A win to el Guerrouj in Athens would be sweet revenge after he tripped over in the Olympic final last year.
El Guerrouj caught Morceli's heels at the bell and he went crashing to the ground along with his gold medal hopes. The Algerian then sprinted away to capture the Olympic 1,500 metres gold medal.
Later in the year El Guerrouj got some minor compensation.
He ran the fastest 1,500 last year with 3:29.05 in Brussels to supplant Said Aouita as the holder of the Moroccan best for the event.
Then he inflicted Morceli's first 1,500 or mile defeat for four years at the Grand Prix final in Milan.
This year he is unbeaten and comfortably sits on top of the 1,500 rankings with his 3:29.30 run in Stockholm on July 7.
He has four of the best five times in the world so far this year.
Into the bargain he got within a fraction of a second of Morceli's world mile best in Oslo on July 4.
Not surprisingly Morceli has assiduously avoided standing on the same start line as El Guerrouj.
A trace of pan-Arab rivalry enters his voice when el Guerrouj talks about Morceli.
"This year my ambitions are simple. I want to win the world championship and break Morceli's 1,500 and mile records.
"Of course I respect Morceli for what he has achieved but I feel I can do even better."
"I am in the shape to break his records but it is all in the hands of Allah," he said.
References to Allah pepper any conversation with El Guerrouj.
A devout muslim, he broke the world indoor 1,500 mark in February in the middle of Ramadan, without having had anything to eat or drink for more than 10 hours.
El Guerrouj has taken the unusual step of moving down a distance since he entered the senior ranks.
He first came to the attention of the athletics world with the fastest 5,000 metres leg at the 1994 World Road Relay championships.
In photographs of the victorious Moroccan celebrations, a fresh-faced El Guerrouj can be seen alongside Olympic champions Brahim Boutayeb and Khalid Skah.
The following winter he made the decision that his forte was his speed rather than his stamina.
In 1995 he became the world indoor 1,500 champion before notching up the silver medal behind Morceli in Gothenburg.
El Guerrouj, almost inevitably, was inspired to take up athletics by the feats of Aouita.
Watching him win the 1984 Olympic 5,000 as a nine-year-old motivated the youngster from Berkan to start running.
"Of course the inspiration to run came from watching Aouita and also later Skah and Boutayeb but I don't feel close to anyone in particular. I am my own character."
After progressing through the Moroccan school system he was promoted to their highly organised national junior squad in 1991 and moved into national athletics training centre near Rabat.
The following year eagle-eyed observers would have seen him picking up the bronze medal over 5,000 at the world junior championships.
The two men in front of him were Ethiopia's Haile Gebrselassie and Kenya's Ismael Kirui.
Both have since gone on to become world champions in the senior ranks. Now perhaps El Guerrouj's own day on top of the medal podium is nigh.
